newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian press sees Clinton free of Jewish lobby.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian press sees Clinton free of Jewish lobby.

text.p: Egyptian government newspapers said on Thursday that U.S. President Bill Clinton's election victory cast him free of the Jewish lobby and one of them predicted confrontation between him and the Israeli government.

"Clinton chose to postpone the confrontation until after the elections," said the main editorial in the newspaper al-Akhbar. "That confrontation, we believe, is to reject extremist positions and provocative policies which jeopardise the security of the region and hence the interests of the United States."
The newspaper said Clinton's hands were tied during the election campaign because of fears that Republican candidate Bob Dole might exploit any chink in his support for Israel.

"It's clear that Israel, and not the Palestinians, is putting problems and obstacles in the way of peace and the Israeli government has tried to take advantage of the U.S. election battle to pressure Clinton," prominent Egyptian journalist Anis Mansour wrote in the Al-Ahram weekly.
"But now Clinton has won and threats and promises no longer affect him because he is keen on peace in the Middle East and to be called a man of peace at the end of it all," he added.
"Now Clinton can say 'no' to the Jewish lobby," wrote veteran journalist Mostafa Amin his column in al-Akhbar.

Netanyahu has angered Arabs by refusing to trade Arab land for peace and by trying to renegotiate a long-delayed agreement under which the Jewish state would redeploy its troops from the Palestinian West Bank town of Hebron.
